# Library
```{r}
library(mikropml) #machine learning pipeline to be used to build predictor model
library(readxl) #used to pull in tables/data from excel
```

# Pull in table form excel
```{r}
Data<- read_excel("NRRRF_anitamox/Anitamox_influent_data_working.xlsx", sheet="Inf only clean MachL")
Data.df<- as.data.frame(Data) #make into data frame for mikropml
```

## preprocessing usingl mikropml
```{r}
Data.p<-mikropml::preprocess_data(Data.df, outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF")
```

## Linear regression
```{r}
results_glmnet<-run_ml(Data.p$dat_transformed, method="glmnet", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, seed=101626)
results_glmnet$feature_importance
results_glmnet$performance
```

## Random forest
```{r}
results_rf<-run_ml(Data.p$dat_transformed, method="rf", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, seed=101626)
results_rf$feature_importance
results_rf$performance
```

## Decision Tree
```{r}
results_dt<-run_ml(Data.p$dat_transformed, method="rpart2", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, seed=101626)
results_dt$feature_importance
results_dt$performance
```

## XG Boost
```{r}
results_xg<-run_ml(Data.p$dat_transformed, method="xgbTree", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, seed=9926)
#this takes very long-run did not complte- will likely be better to just stick to glmnet, dt, and rf like in savannas paper. 
```


# Reduced feature model- chem data only w/ config categories
```{r}
Datar<- read_excel("NRRRF_anitamox/Anitamox_influent_data_working.xlsx", sheet="Inf only clean MachL reduced")
Datar.df<- as.data.frame(Datar) #make into data frame for mikropml
```

## preprocessing usingl mikropml
```{r}
Datar.p<-mikropml::preprocess_data(Datar.df, outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF")
```

## Linear regression
```{r}
results_glmnet_r<-run_ml(Datar.p$dat_transformed, method="glmnet", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=4, seed=101626) #using kfold=4 because it has to be between 1 and number of features
results_glmnet_r$feature_importance
results_glmnet_r$performance # did not do a particularly good job with data only up to Dec2, but adding data up to Mar 17 got R2 to 0.5466, adding data up to Oct 6 push R2 backward to .36797
```

## Random forest
```{r}
results_rf_r<-run_ml(Datar.p$dat_transformed, method="rf", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=4, seed=101626)
results_rf_r$feature_importance
results_rf_r$performance
#this gives an R2 of 0.597. RMSE and MAE are still kinda high but this the best R2 we've gotten so far., done only with data up to December 2 
# gives R2 of 0.6788 when data up to Mar 17 is added, gives R2 of .3629597 with data up to Oct 6th
```

## Decision Tree
```{r}
results_dt_r<-run_ml(Datar.p$dat_transformed, method="rpart2", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=4, seed=101626)
results_dt_r$feature_importance
results_dt_r$performance
# when data up to MAR 17 is added Decision tree is best with R2 of 0.7171 and a lower RMSE and MAE than linear and rf. With data up to Oct 6th, R2 is .4204528, better than rf and lr but likely need to tune some hyperparameters and gett he microbial data in. 
```

# Effluent only features W/ config categories
```{r}
DataE<- read_excel("NRRRF_anitamox/Anitamox_influent_data_working.xlsx", sheet="Eff only clean MachL")
DataE.df<- as.data.frame(DataE) #make into data frame for mikropml
```

## preprocessing usingl mikropml
```{r}
DataE.p<-mikropml::preprocess_data(DataE.df, outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF")
```

## Linear regression
```{r}
results_glmnet_E<-run_ml(DataE.p$dat_transformed, method="glmnet", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=5, seed=101626) 
results_glmnet_E$feature_importance
results_glmnet_E$performance # with data up to Oct 6, gives R2 of .9873273, RMSE and MAE are kinda high though, microbial data may help to improve them. 
```

## Random forest
```{r}
results_rf_E<-run_ml(DataE.p$dat_transformed, method="rf", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=5, seed=101626)
results_rf_E$feature_importance
results_rf_E$performance # with data up to Oct 6, R2 is .9787831, slightly lower than lr and with higher errors
```

## Decision Tree
```{r}
results_dt_E<-run_ml(DataE.p$dat_transformed, method="rpart2", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=5, seed=101626)
results_dt_E$feature_importance
results_dt_E$performance # with data up to Oct 6, R2 is .7299559, worst between RF and LR, and with mucher higher errors. still performing better on both metrics than influent only data. 
```

# Effluent only reduced data
```{r}
DataE2<- read_excel("NRRRF_anitamox/Anitamox_influent_data_working.xlsx", sheet="Eff only clean MachL 2")
DataE2.df<- as.data.frame(DataE2) #make into data frame for mikropml
```

## preprocessing usingl mikropml
```{r}
DataE2.p<-mikropml::preprocess_data(DataE2.df, outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF")
```

## Linear regression
```{r}
results_glmnet_E2<-run_ml(DataE2.p$dat_transformed, method="glmnet", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=2, seed=102026) #kfold at 2 due to number of features
results_glmnet_E2$feature_importance
results_glmnet_E2$performance # with data up to Oct 6, gives R2 of .744504
```

## Random forest
```{r}
results_rf_E2<-run_ml(DataE2.p$dat_transformed, method="rf", outcome_colname="AmmoniaEFF", find_feature_importance=TRUE, kfold=2, seed=102026)
results_rf_E2$feature_importance
results_rf_E2$performance # with data up to Oct 6, R2 is .7542735, slightly lower than lr and with higher errors
```
